chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Sa'd bin Abdullah told us, from al-Haytham bin Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, who said: Al-Husayn bin 'Alwan told us, from 'Amr bin Khalid, from Zayd bin Ali, from his father Ali bin al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn, from his father Ali bin Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
A beast is a jubar, a well is a jubar, a metal mine is a jubar, and in rikaz is the khums. And the jubar is the hadr (killing in vain) for which there is no indemnity (diyah) nor retaliation (qad').

key_terms.الرِّكَاز: Al-Rikaz: Treasure trove or buried wealth, subject to the khums tax.
key_terms.الْخُمُس: Al-Khums: The one-fifth portion of certain gains or treasures payable to the Imam.
key_terms.الْقَوْد: Al-Qad': Retaliation in kind (eye for an eye) in cases of intentional homicide or injury.
key_terms.الْمَعْدِن: Al-Ma'din: A mine or source of minerals/metals.
key_terms.الْهَدْر: Al-Hadr: A specific type of accidental death/killing in Islamic law, often implying no financial compensation.
key_terms.جَبَّار: Jubar: A legal term for accidental killing or damage where no full compensation or retaliation is due.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Jubar and Hadr in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain to define 'jubar' as accidental death where no blood money (diyah) or retaliation (qad') is due, citing the beast, well, and mine as primary examples. The hadith further clarifies that 'jubar' equates to 'hadr' (a specific category of accidental killing) and links the concept to the obligation of khums on rikaz (treasure trove), reflecting the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding liability in non-intentional harm.
